guideTitle: 6 Best Emerson Smart Alarm Clocks in 2026
metaTitle: Best Emerson Smart Alarm Clocks in 2026
metaDescription: Six Emerson SmartSet clock radios compared on display size, Bluetooth, USB and wireless charging, and gradual wake-up so you can pick the right one.
introParagraphs: Emerson's SmartSet line is built around one idea: the clock sets its own time, date and daylight saving, so it recovers by itself after a power cut. That single feature removes the most common bedside clock failure, which is waking up to a blinking 12:00 or an alarm that quietly shifted an hour after the clocks changed.

Around that core, the family splits into plain radio clocks, Bluetooth speakers and models with a wireless charging pad on top. We compared six distinct SmartSet models: the Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM, the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio, the Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker, the Emerson SmartSet Wireless Charging Dual Alarm Clock Radio 10W, the Emerson CKS1401 and the Emerson CKSW5010. Listing variants of the same product were counted once, and everything is evaluated based on product specs and buyer feedback.
WorthRated cares about clocks that stay easy to live with, so the sections below weigh display size, extras and how much you actually need beyond a reliable alarm.

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM
products.description:
This is the core Emerson SmartSet clock radio, and it does the essentials without extras. SmartSet sets the correct year, month, date, day and time automatically, and it keeps them right after a power interruption. Digital PLL AM/FM tuning comes with 20 memory presets, plus a sleep timer and a snooze button. Two alarms let you wake to the radio or a buzzer on different schedules.

The 0.9 inch jade green LED has a dimmer, so it stays readable across the room without lighting up the bedroom. Because the clock has no Bluetooth or charging features, there is less to set up and less that can go wrong. The tradeoff is that the display is the smaller size in this family, and anyone who wants to stream a podcast or charge a phone will need to look further down the list.

In daily use you plug it in, tune a station and set the alarm, which takes about as long as reading the sentence. Compared with the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth at 1.4 inches, this model has a smaller display and no wireless audio. Compared with the CKS1401 and its USB-C port, it is just as simple but lacks the gradual wake-up. It is the clock to hand to someone who has never wanted a smart device.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a plain, self-setting clock radio with no extras.

AM/FM radio with 20 memory presets for quick tuning
Dimmer keeps the green LED gentle at night
Few features means less to set up and troubleshoot
cons: 0.9 inch display is the smaller size in this family
No Bluetooth streaming or phone charging at all

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio
products.description:
The Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio adds wireless audio and a bigger display to the family. It uses Bluetooth 5.1 with a range of up to 10 meters, so phones and tablets can stream music and podcasts to the built-in speaker. The bold 1.4 inch orange LED has 3 brightness levels and an auto-dim mode that follows the room light.

SmartSet recovers the time automatically after power interruptions and adjusts for daylight saving. A USB port offers 1.5A at 5V for topping up a phone overnight. The listing mentions FM radio, and the same clock appears in more than one listing variant, which we count as a single product.

Ownership is about pairing a phone once and then forgetting about it. Compared with the base AM/FM model and its 0.9 inch display, the Bluetooth model is easier to read and plays your own audio. Compared with the wireless charging models, it asks you to plug a cable in rather than just set the phone down. At 1.5A its USB port is weaker than the 2.1A on the Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker, so a tablet will charge slowly.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a large readable display and Bluetooth streaming without wireless charging.
pros: 1.4 inch orange display is easy to read from bed
Bluetooth 5.1 reaches about 10 meters from the clock
Auto-dim adapts the glow to the light in the room
USB port tops up a phone overnight at 1.5A
cons: Charging needs a cable, not a pad
More setup than the plain radio clock

products.name: Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker
products.description:
This Emerson SmartSet clock radio combines a Bluetooth speaker with a USB port and a 1.4 inch display. It uses Bluetooth V4.1 for pairing and streaming. The USB output is rated 2.1A at 5V, and an included button cell battery keeps time and alarm settings through a short outage.

It also carries digital tuning FM with 20 station memories. The older Bluetooth version means a less modern feature list than the 5.1 models, but pairing is still straightforward. On paper the USB output is the strongest in the family, at 2.1A versus 1.5A on the newer Bluetooth clock.

In practice it behaves like a classic clock radio that can also play your phone. Compared with the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth at version 5.1 and 1.5A, this one has older Bluetooth but a stronger USB output. Compared with the wireless charging models, it is simpler and cable based. The battery backup is worth noting because several of the other picks do not mention one in their listings.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants Bluetooth and faster USB charging in a classic clock radio.
pros: USB port is rated 2.1A at 5V for faster charging
Button cell battery keeps time and alarm settings
Digital FM tuning with 20 station memories
1.4 inch display is easy to read at night
cons: Older Bluetooth V4.1 standard than the other models
No wireless charging pad on top

products.name: Emerson SmartSet Wireless Charging Dual Alarm Clock Radio 10W
products.description:
This Emerson SmartSet model puts a 10 watt Qi wireless charger on top of the clock, so you drop your phone on it to charge. It adds a USB port rated 2.1A at 5V for tablets or a second device. Bluetooth 5.1 handles pairing, and an aux input is listed for wired audio.

The pad turns the clock into a charging station, which cuts down on cables at the bedside. You need a phone that supports Qi, and a thick case can reduce or block charging. The listing describes PLL FM, so there is no AM band in this version, which matters if you listen to AM news or sports.

Ownership centers on keeping the pad clear and the phone aligned so charging actually starts. Compared with the 15W Emerson CKSW5010, the 10W pad is slower. Compared with the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio at 1.5A USB, it swaps a cable for a pad and keeps a stronger 2.1A port as a backup. If you already own a Qi phone, this is the least costly way into the pad design.
products.bestFor: Anyone with a Qi phone who wants one bedside station for clock, speaker and charging.
pros: Ten watt Qi pad charges a phone by dropping it on
USB port adds 2.1A for a second device or tablet
Bluetooth 5.1 pairs easily with phones
Aux input supports wired audio sources
cons: Needs a Qi-compatible phone and a thin case
FM only, with no AM band listed

products.name: Emerson CKS1401 Smartset AM/FM Dual Alarm Clock Radio
products.description:
The Emerson CKS1401 is a SmartSet clock radio with a graduated wake-up feature that gently increases the alarm volume. It has a 0.9 inch white LED display with a 4-level dimmer: high, medium, medium low and low. The SmartSet system sets year, month, date, day and time as soon as you plug it in.

The gradual alarm is the reason to choose it, because it eases you awake instead of starting at full volume. The display is the smaller 0.9 inch size, and the listing mentions a USB-C port. There is no Bluetooth in the listing, so this clock plays radio and alarms only.

In practice it is the calm, simple choice for people who dislike sudden alarms. Compared with the Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM, it adds gradual wake-up and USB-C at the same display size. Compared with the CKSW5010, it skips Bluetooth and wireless charging in favor of simplicity. Heavy sleepers should note that a slow ramp can feel too gentle, so check how loud it finally gets.
products.bestFor: People who want a gentle volume ramp and a clean white display without extra features.
pros: Alarm volume rises gradually instead of blasting
Four-level dimmer runs from high down to low
SmartSet sets the time the moment it is plugged in
USB-C port suits modern phone cables
cons: Smaller 0.9 inch display than the Bluetooth models
No Bluetooth listed, so no wireless audio

products.name: Emerson CKSW5010 Smartset Wireless Charging Clock
products.description:
The Emerson CKSW5010 is the most feature-packed clock in this lineup. It offers 15 watt ultra-fast wireless charging with a lift-up stand so you can see the phone while it charges. A 3 watt charging area handles AirPods. Bluetooth 5.3 gives pairing at up to 10 meters.

SmartSet sets the date and time automatically as soon as you plug it in and after every power interruption. The charging features make it a hub for the nightstand. It is also the most complex model here, and it needs a Qi-compatible phone with a case thin enough to charge through.

Ownership is mainly about leaving the phone on the stand overnight and the earbuds on their spot. Compared with the 10W Emerson model, it charges faster at 15W. Compared with the Emerson CKS1401, it adds Bluetooth and charging but drops the gradual wake-up. It carries the newest Bluetooth in the family at 5.3, so it is the one most likely to stay current.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants fast wireless charging, earbud charging and Bluetooth in one clock.
pros: Fifteen watt wireless charging is the fastest here
Lift-up stand lets you see the phone while charging
Three watt area charges AirPods alongside the phone
Newest Bluetooth 5.3 in the family reaches 10 meters
cons: Most complex of the six to learn and place
Needs a Qi-compatible phone with a thin case

buyingCriteria.explanation: Emerson SmartSet models range from a 0.9 inch display on the AM/FM and CKS1401 clocks to 1.4 inches on the Bluetooth models. Colors differ too, with jade green, blue, white and orange options across the family. A larger display is easier to read from the pillow, but every display needs a dimmer so it does not glare in a dark room. The Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth offers 3 levels plus auto-dim, and the Emerson CKS1401 offers 4 levels. Choose by how far the clock sits from your head and how sensitive you are to light at night.

SmartSet is the reason to buy an Emerson, because the clock sets year, month, date, day and time by itself and recovers after a power cut. It also adjusts for daylight saving, which removes the twice-yearly chore. All six models here use it, so it does not separate the picks, but it separates this brand from cheaper no-name clocks. The Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker adds a button cell battery on top, which protects alarm settings through a short outage. Check that the model you pick lists SmartSet in the title or features before you buy.

Bluetooth lets you stream podcasts and music from a phone to the clock speaker. The Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth and the 10W wireless charging model list version 5.1, the CKSW5010 lists 5.3 with up to 10 meters, and the older speaker clock lists V4.1. Newer versions tend to pair faster and hold a steadier connection through a bedroom wall. If you never stream audio, you can skip Bluetooth entirely and save the pairing steps. The Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM and the CKS1401 are the two picks without it.

Emerson offers USB ports, USB-C and wireless pads, and the numbers differ more than the pictures suggest. The Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth provides 1.5A, the older speaker clock gives 2.1A, the 10W model adds a Qi pad and the CKSW5010 reaches 15W with 3W for AirPods. Wireless charging requires a Qi phone and a case that is not too thick, so check your case before paying for the pad. A USB port is the more universal choice, and 2.1A or more is the number to look for if a tablet will charge overnight.

The Emerson CKS1401 uses a graduated wake-up that gently increases alarm volume until you stir. It is a good fit for people who dislike sudden alarms or share a room with someone who sleeps later. Models without it start at the set volume, which is fine for heavy sleepers but harsh for light ones. If you want a gentle start, confirm the feature is listed before you buy, because the other five Emerson picks here do not claim it. Pair it with the 4-level dimmer so the morning light is gentle too.

All six include radio, but the details differ in ways that matter if you actually listen. The Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM has AM/FM with 20 presets, the CKS1401 is AM/FM, and the wireless charging models list PLL FM only. If you want AM for news or sports, confirm the band is listed before choosing a charging model. PLL tuning is described as steadier than older dial tuning, with less drift once a station is set. Twenty presets are plenty for most households, so count your stations rather than chasing a bigger number.

howWeEvaluated.title: Core clock function
howWeEvaluated.description: Every model here uses SmartSet, so we compared how the rest of each clock behaves around that core. The Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM and the CKS1401 keep things simple, while the others add speakers and chargers. We looked for features that protect settings through power cuts, such as the button cell on the older speaker clock, and treated that as part of reliability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Display readability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sizes, colors and dimming because a bedroom clock is read half-asleep. The Bluetooth models offer 1.4 inch displays, while the AM/FM and CKS1401 offer 0.9 inch displays. The CKS1401 provides a 4-level dimmer and the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth gives 3 levels plus auto-dim, so each has a different way to avoid glare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connectivity
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed Bluetooth version and range, since a newer version generally means easier pairing. The CKSW5010 lists 5.3, the Bluetooth and 10W models list 5.1, and the older speaker clock lists V4.1. Two picks have no Bluetooth at all, and we scored them on simplicity instead of connectivity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared USB output and wireless power: 1.5A, 2.1A, 10W and 15W. The CKSW5010 also charges earbuds at 3W, which no other pick here matches. We also considered how forgiving each design is, since a Qi pad needs a compatible phone and case while a USB port works with nearly any device.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The base AM/FM model is the simplest, the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth has the best display, the older speaker clock has the strongest USB at 2.1A, the 10W model is the entry wireless charger, the CKS1401 has the gentlest wake-up and the CKSW5010 is the most complete. Each pick leads on one spec, so the right choice depends on your single most-used feature.

faq.q: Which Emerson alarm clock is best?
faq.a: For most people the Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth Dual Alarm Clock Radio is a good balance, with a 1.4 inch display and Bluetooth 5.1. If you want the simplest option, take the Emerson SmartSet Dual Alarm Clock Radio AM/FM. If you want fast charging, choose the Emerson CKSW5010 at 15W.

It sets the year, month, date, day and time automatically when you plug in and after power interruptions. It also adjusts for daylight saving. That removes most of the manual setup and the usual wrong-time surprise after an outage.

faq.q: Do I need a Qi phone for wireless charging?
faq.a: Yes, the 10W model and the CKSW5010 at 15W need a Qi-compatible phone. A very thick case can also interfere with charging. If you are unsure, pick a USB model such as the Emerson Smartset Alarm Clock Radio with Bluetooth Speaker at 2.1A instead.

faq.q: Is Bluetooth worth it on a clock radio?
faq.a: It is if you stream podcasts or music at bedtime. The Emerson SmartSet Bluetooth lists 5.1 with 10 meters, and the CKSW5010 lists 5.3. If you only listen to the radio, skip it and save yourself the pairing steps.

faq.q: Does gradual wake-up work for heavy sleepers?
faq.a: The Emerson CKS1401 raises the alarm volume gradually, which suits light sleepers best. Heavy sleepers should check that the final volume is loud enough to rouse them. A slow ramp that never gets loud enough can lead to missed alarms.

faq.q: Are the different listings the same clock?
faq.a: Some listings are variants of one product, such as the two Bluetooth listings with the 1.4 inch orange LED. We counted them once. Check the model name and features before buying so you get the display size and charging you expect.

faq.q: How do I maintain these clocks?
faq.a: Keep the vents dust free and replace the backup battery on models that use one. Wipe the wireless charging pad clean so nothing blocks the coil. Unplug the clock during storms to protect it from surges.
